summary: The note describes the Free Soil Party, a short-lived United States political party that competed in the 1848 and 1852 presidential elections and some state elections. It was a single-issue party whose main aim was to stop slavery from expanding into the Western territories, on the argument that free labor on free soil was morally and economically superior. It also sometimes sought repeal of laws discriminating against freed African Americans, as in Ohio.
one_line: The Free Soil Party was a short-lived single-issue US party opposing the expansion of slavery into Western territories in the 1848 and 1852 elections.
key_facts: The Free Soil Party was a short-lived political party in the United States.
The Free Soil Party was active in the 1848 and 1852 presidential elections.
The Free Soil Party was also active in some state elections.
The Free Soil Party was a single-issue party.
The main purpose of the Free Soil Party was to oppose the expansion of slavery into the Western territories.
The Free Soil Party argued that free men on free soil constituted a morally and economically superior system to slavery.
The Free Soil Party sometimes worked to remove existing laws that discriminated against freed African Americans.
The Free Soil Party sometimes sought to remove discriminatory laws against freed African Americans in states such as Ohio.
